synonyms: tractus tegmentalis centralis ; CTT ; central tract of tegmentum

Definition: Descending extrapyramidal motor tract arising from the red nucleus of the midbrain tegmentum; decussates immediately in the ventral tegmental decussation and descends in the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord to facilitate flexor muscle tone and modulate distal limb movements. Prominent and functionally critical in non-human primates; considerably reduced in humans where corticospinal input to the red nucleus partially substitutes its role. Difficult to isolate in human DTI due to its small cross-section.

Descending extrapyramidal pathway from the vestibular nuclei of the medulla to the spinal cord; mediates postural reflexes and extensor muscle tone in response to head position and movement. Composed of two divisions: the lateral vestibulospinal tract (from Deiters nucleus, uncrossed, full spinal extent) facilitating extensor tone, and the medial vestibulospinal tract (bilateral, restricted to cervical cord) coordinating head and neck posture via the medial longitudinal fasciculus.
synonyms: tractus vestibulospinalis ; lateral vestibulospinal tract ; medial vestibulospinal tract ; VST

Definition: Descending extrapyramidal tract from the superior colliculus of the midbrain tectum; decussates in the dorsal tegmental decussation (fountain decussation of Meynert) and descends in the anterior funiculus of the cervical spinal cord to coordinate reflexive head and eye movements toward contralateral visual stimuli. Functionally important for orienting responses; closely associated with tecto-reticular projections.

A diffuse periventricular visceral pathway running along the floor of the fourth ventricle and the periaqueductal gray; connects the hypothalamus with parasympathetic and sympathetic preganglionic nuclei throughout the brainstem and contains reciprocal ascending and descending autonomic fibers. Also called Schütz's bundle. Distinct from the medial longitudinal fasciculus: the DLF is a visceral/autonomic tract whereas the MLF is a somatic/oculomotor tract.
synonyms: Schütz bundle ; Schütz's bundle ; DLF ; fasciculus longitudinalis dorsalis ; posterior longitudinal fasciculus ; bundle of Schütz

Definition: A looping white matter bundle exiting the ventral medial globus pallidus internus; curves ventrally around the posterior limb of the internal capsule and rostrally into the subthalamic region to join the thalamic fasciculus (Field H1 of Forel) before entering the motor thalamus. Together with the lenticular fasciculus it constitutes the primary output pathway of the basal ganglia. The two bundles are anatomically complementary routes around and through the internal capsule respectively.
synonyms: AL ; ansa peduncularis ; ansa lenticularis in thalamo ; ansa lenticularis in thalamus ; ventral peduncle of lateral forebrain bundle

Definition: A compact bundle of myelinated fibers from the globus pallidus internus that passes directly through (rather than around) the posterior limb of the internal capsule and traverses the subthalamic region as Field H2 of Forel before merging with the ansa lenticularis to form the thalamic fasciculus (Field H1). Its straight trajectory through the capsule distinguishes it anatomically from the looping ansa lenticularis.
synonyms: Field H2 of Forel ; H2 field ; pallidothalamic tract ; lenticular bundle ; fasciculus lenticularis ; Forel field H2

Definition: The merged pallidothalamic pathway (Field H1 of Forel) formed by the convergence of the ansa lenticularis and lenticular fasciculus in the prerubral field; ascends into the ventral anterior and ventral lateral thalamic nuclei to relay basal ganglia motor output to the motor cortex via the thalamocortical projection. The key bottleneck of the indirect basal ganglia output pathway and a target for DBS in Parkinson disease.
synonyms: Field H1 of Forel ; H1 field ; Forel field H1 ; fasciculus thalamicus ; pallidothalamic tract (merged) ; FT

Definition: A recently isolated short-range association pathway connecting posterior temporal cortex (superior temporal gyrus / temporal-parietal junction) with the inferior parietal lobule in an oblique aslant orientation; proposed to play a role in visuospatial processing and mirror-neuron networks by analogy with the frontal aslant tract. First described by Parlatini et al. (2017) and Weiner et al. (2017). No SNOMED or UBERON ontology entry currently exists; classification is tractography-atlas-defined only.

The anteriorly convex bend of the internal capsule lying between the anterior and posterior limbs; contains corticobulbar fibers projecting from the motor cortex to the cranial nerve motor nuclei of the brainstem (particularly CN VII lower face, CN IX, CN X, CN XII), along with some corticospinal fibers to the cervical cord. Clinically critical: a small lacunar infarct at the genu can produce contralateral central facial palsy and dysarthria disproportionate to limb weakness.
synonyms: genu capsulae internae ; knee of internal capsule ; internal capsule genu ; GENU-IC

Definition: The portion of the internal capsule passing beneath the lentiform nucleus; contains the acoustic radiations from the medial geniculate nucleus to the primary auditory cortex (Heschl's gyrus) and the ventral component of the optic radiations (Meyer's loop) from the lateral geniculate nucleus sweeping anteriorly through the temporal lobe. Damage produces auditory and visual field deficits depending on extent of involvement; the acoustic radiation component is particularly susceptible in temporal lobe surgery.
synonyms: sublenticular limb of internal capsule ; sublenticular internal capsule ; SLIC

Definition: The anterior ventral subdivision of the optic radiation carrying upper visual field signals (lower retinal fibers) from the lateral geniculate nucleus; curves anteriorly into the temporal lobe white matter before turning posteriorly to reach the inferior bank of the calcarine sulcus in the primary visual cortex. The most anterior extent of Meyer's loop determines the minimum safe resection margin in anterior temporal lobectomy for epilepsy; damage produces a contralateral superior quadrantanopia ('pie in the sky' defect). Also called the temporal loop of the optic radiation.
synonyms: inferior optic radiation ; Meyer loop ; temporal loop of optic radiation ; anterior optic radiation ; archambault loop ; inferior bundle of optic radiation

Definition: The posterior dorsal subdivision of the optic radiation carrying lower visual field signals (upper retinal fibers) from the lateral geniculate nucleus; travels directly through the parietal lobe white matter to the superior bank of the calcarine sulcus in the primary visual cortex without the anterior temporal excursion of Meyer's loop. Damage produces a contralateral inferior quadrantanopia. Less commonly referenced by name in the clinical literature than Meyer's loop; the eponym derives from Franz Baum who described the parietal component distinct from the temporal loop.
synonyms: superior optic radiation ; parietal loop of optic radiation ; dorsal optic radiation ; posterior optic radiation

Definition: The larger of the two terminal branches of the olfactory tract at the olfactory trigone; courses laterally across the anterior perforated substance to terminate in the primary olfactory cortex (piriform cortex), the periamygdaloid cortex, and the entorhinal cortex. Carries the principal olfactory projection to limbic and memory-related cortices. The lateral stria is larger and more prominent than the medial stria and is the dominant output pathway of the olfactory tract.
synonyms: lateral root of olfactory tract ; stria olfactoria lateralis ; tractus olfactorius lateralis

Definition: The smaller of the two terminal branches of the olfactory tract at the olfactory trigone; courses medially across the anterior perforated substance toward the medial olfactory area (subcallosal gyrus and septal nuclei), carrying olfactory signals to the contralateral olfactory bulb via the anterior commissure and to the medial septal area and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis. Less prominent than the lateral stria and not consistently resolvable in standard DTI.
synonyms: medial root of olfactory tract ; stria olfactoria medialis ; tractus olfactorius medialis

Definition: A short-range association tract recently isolated alongside the frontal aslant tract (FAT) connecting the orbitofrontal cortex with lateral prefrontal areas in an oblique aslant orientation; proposed to support emotional regulation, reward-based decision-making, and the integration of affective and cognitive control signals. First characterized in detail by Catani et al. and colleagues using tractography dissection methods. No SNOMED or UBERON ontology entry exists; classification is tractography-atlas-defined only. Distinct from the FAT, which connects SMA/pre-SMA to the inferior frontal gyrus.
synonyms: FOAT ; fronto-orbital aslant tract ; orbital aslant tract
